newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium nearby premiums flare, LME watch market.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium nearby premiums flare, LME watch market.

text.p: Prompt backwardations for aluminium flared during early Tuesday LME ring trading, underpinning the general cash/threes premium, with Exchange authorities monitoring the activity.

The 'TOM/NEXT' (tomorrow/next day) backwardation, which represents belated business against Monday's prompt date, traded out from $15 to $20, ending the session at $5. On Monday, this comparable date was the August "third Wednesday", and was trading at $5.
"The August date was the key date in aluminium, so we were watching how it performed," LME Chief Executive David King said.
Cash/threes traded out to $60 backwardation - double the levels that prevailed late last week, with many of the tight positions having being being rolled forward into September, traders said.
The tightness is thus expected to continue, as many shorts have simply put off the day of reckoning, they added.
The three months market was largely neglected and unmoved by the spread business, trading arounf slightly softer pre-market levels of $1,665.
